name: Can I replace a walk-in shower with a bathtub after removal?

mainEntity.name: Can I replace a walk-in shower with a bathtub after removal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a shower with a bathtub depends on available bathroom footprint, drain placement, and plumbing configurations. A standard alcove bathtub typically requires an opening roughly sixty inches long and thirty to thirty-two inches wide. If your existing walk-in shower is smaller, adjacent walls or vanities may need modification to accommodate the tub. Additionally, showers often use two-inch drain lines, whereas standard tub drains are one-and-a-half inches, so the plumbing rough-in under the subfloor must be adapted to align with the new tub waste-and-overflow layout.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, if your bathroom footprint accommodates tub dimensions and the plumbing drain lines are adapted under the floor to align with the new tub waste assembly.
